subject: gracie
prompt: The attached photos show Gracie, one real adult raccoon. The last photo shows two raccoons: Gracie is the one at the back, standing in three-quarter view and looking at the camera; the raccoon in front is a different raccoon, so ignore it. That photo is her clearest standing view and the best guide to her pale, greyer, shaggier lower body. Draw a clean character turnaround of her for 3D modelling: four full-body views of the same raccoon in one 2x2 grid, each view centred in its own quarter of the image with a wide margin: top-left FRONT view (facing the viewer), top-right THREE-QUARTER front view (facing front-left), bottom-left SIDE profile (facing left), bottom-right BACK view. Neutral standing pose on all four legs, legs straight and apart, all four paws visible on one ground line, tail held out behind and slightly down, not crossing the body. Same size and scale in every view. Flat, even, shadowless studio light: no cast shadows, no ground shadow, no rim light. Plain uniform light grey background. No text, no numbers, no labels, no grid lines. Keep her identity exactly. Most important, her signature: the fur on her lower body (belly, flanks and hindquarters, down over her legs) is lighter, greyer and noticeably longer and shaggier than the shorter, darker fur on her back, so her underside and legs look fluffy and pale grey. Also keep her full dark eye mask with pale brows and a pale muzzle, rounded ears with pale rims, a ringed tail with dark and light bands, long-fingered hand-like front paws with dark palms, and plantigrade hind feet with dark soles, pale toes and pale fur over the top of the foot. True-to-life raccoon proportions. The style bible's character look, as in Stevie's approved turnaround: very high-quality naturalistic rendering with soft, believable fur and anatomy; fine, soft, naturalistic fur with fur strands at every silhouette edge; high detail on her face, mask and banded tail; no visible brushwork; never photographic and never painterly.
